title: OpenFGA Foundations
subtitle: Zanzibar tuples, DSL models, and check
content:
🕸️ Tuples Are the Policy

OpenFGA stores relationship tuples — (user, relation, object) — and a model defines which relations exist and how they imply each other. Authorization = graph reachability. The canonical docs model (verified Sept 2026):

OpenFGA DSL: viewer defined via editor (concentric) + team indirection 
# Last verified: 2026-09 vs openfga.dev direct-relationships
model
  schema 1.1

type user

type team
  relations
    define member: [user]

type document
  relations
    define viewer: [user, team#member] or editor
    define editor: [user, team#member]

# Tuples (written at share-time):
# anne editor document:Q3        -> anne can view via concentric inherit
# team:eng member cara           -> cara in the team
# team:eng editor document:Q3    -> whole team edits (and hence views)
# Last verified: 2026-09 vs openfga.dev direct-relationships model schema 1.1 type user type team relations define member: [user] type document relations define viewer: [user, team#member] or editor define editor: [user, team#member] # Tuples (written at share-time): # anne editor document:Q3 -> anne can view via concentric inherit # team:eng member cara -> cara in the team # team:eng editor document:Q3 -> whole team edits (and hence views)

🔍 check() Reads the Graph

check(user:anne, viewer, document:Q3) walks: direct viewer tuple? team#member path? editor path? Any path → allow. No path → deny. Concentric viewer: ... or editor means editors never need separate viewer tuples — the model bakes the implication in.

Check evaluation as path-finding 
# check(user:anne, viewer, document:Q3)  -> true
#   path: anne --editor--> document:Q3, editor => viewer
# check(user:zoe, viewer, document:Q3)   -> false (no path, default deny)
# check(user:cara, viewer, document:Q3)  -> true
#   path: cara --member--> team:eng --editor--> document:Q3 => viewer
# check(user:anne, viewer, document:Q3) -> true # path: anne --editor--> document:Q3, editor => viewer # check(user:zoe, viewer, document:Q3) -> false (no path, default deny) # check(user:cara, viewer, document:Q3) -> true # path: cara --member--> team:eng --editor--> document:Q3 => viewer

🔍 Critical Review Notes

  • user:* (public wildcard) exists in the DSL for genuinely public objects — but every * in a model deserves a review comment explaining why that object class is public.
  • Contextual tuples (time windows, IP ranges) are evaluated at check-time and are not supported in the playground — integration-test them against a real server (Lesson 14).
  • Model versioning matters: changing define lines changes every past tuple's meaning. Version models like code and migrate tuples deliberately.
🎮 Try it in the Policy Lab → Run the three check scenarios: direct editor, stranger, and team-transitive access. Use the controls under the canvas to switch scenarios and watch the verdict change.

questions.question: What is stored in OpenFGA as the source of truth for access?

options.text: Relationship tuples (user, relation, object) interpreted through a versioned model
Signed JWTs (authentication artifacts, not relationship facts)

questions.explanation: Zanzibar's insight: access = graph reachability over stored relationships. The model defines relation meanings; tuples are the facts.

questions.question: Given define viewer: [user] or editor, anne holds only an editor tuple on doc:Q3. check(anne, viewer, doc:Q3)?

options.text: false — she needs a separate viewer tuple
error — models cannot reference other relations

questions.explanation: Concentric inheritance is the documented pattern: define viewer as editor (plus direct grants) so one tuple serves both.

questions.question: cara is member of team:eng; team:eng is editor of doc:Q3; viewer includes team#member-or-editor paths. check(cara, viewer, doc:Q3)?
questions.explanation: team#member indirection resolves transitively — and check() is path-finding: any valid path from subject to object through allowed relations is an allow.

questions.question: No tuple path exists between subject and object. Verdict?

options.text: Deny — ReBAC default-deny (no path, no access)

questions.explanation: Same invariant as every model in this course: unmatched → deny. ReBAC just spells 'matched' as 'a path exists'.

questions.question: You change define viewer to remove the editor clause. What must you consider?

options.text: Every existing editor tuple silently loses viewer access — model edits are migrations

questions.explanation: The model gives meaning to all stored tuples. Editing defines retroactively reinterprets history — version and migrate deliberately.

questions.question: You add define owner: [user] to document but no rule references owner. Effect?

options.text: None until referenced — the model defines vocabulary; tuples and paths give it meaning

questions.explanation: Unused definitions are inert. Model edits only matter where relations are referenced — which is why edits need review.

questions.question: check() traverses six hops through nested teams. Operational concern?

options.text: Latency and depth limits — flatten hot paths, cache carefully, test p99
More tuples always make it faster

questions.explanation: Reachability cost grows with depth. Production graphs need the same latency budgeting as any hot path.

questions.question: The team is deleted in the IdP but its OpenFGA tuples were never removed. Access via those paths?

options.text: Allow until the tuples are deleted — stale tuples are lingering grants; reconcile via sync/outbox
Deny automatically once the IdP object is gone

questions.explanation: Tuples are independent stored facts — deleting the IdP object does not delete them. Stale tuples resolve and allow: tuple hygiene (sync job/outbox) is part of offboarding.
